chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Washa, who said:
I heard Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about singing.
So he said: It is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
And from the people is one who buys amusing discourse to lead astray from Allah’s Way.

key_terms.الْغِنَاءِ: Singing or vocal music, often distinguished from simple recitation
key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: The path of God, indicating the spiritual direction or way of life
key_terms.لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ: Amusing discourse or diverting talk, used here to describe the nature of singing

ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic basis for the prohibition of singing in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) identifies *al-ghina'* (singing) with *lahw al-hadith* (diverting discourse), citing Surah Luqman 31:6 to establish its capacity to mislead from the path of God. This interpretation is foundational in Shia jurisprudence, where *lahw* is understood not merely as idle talk but as music or vocal art that distracts the heart from spiritual contemplation and divine remembrance.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Washa who said,

‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the singing (music), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘These are the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
And from the people is one who buys amusing discourse to lead astray from Allah’s Way’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Washsha’ who has said the following: “I once heard abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying that once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, was asked about music (and singing).
He (the Imam) said, ’It is in the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘
. . . among people there are those who buy useless things in the form of words to mislead others from the path of Allah.’”
